subject: On-prem gateway deployment & control/data runway alignment
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@greenpeak.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: karty_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: GreenPeak on-prem gateway: initial asks and diagram request

Hi Sergio / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. GreenPeak is planning an on-prem gateway deployment at two colo sites (SJC + IAD) and we'd like to align on the control-plane / data-plane demarc and the runway for a controlled canary. High level asks:

- Confirm the expected control-plane endpoints (FQDNs) and whether those must be NATed behind our edge IPs.
- Clarify outbound egress endpoints for telemetry and metrics (port/IP allowlist).
- Recommended certificate lifecycle and KMS/HSM integration points for token exchange.
- Any constraints for BGP vs static routing for the data plane (we prefer BGP but can do static).
- Expected attachment diagrams and VLAN tags so our NOC can prep.

Can you share your reference topology diagram and a short runbook snapshot? We'd like a 30-minute alignment call this week if possible. I'm attaching a short doc with our internal asks.

Attachments: greenpeak-deploy-asks.docx (deployment checklist / VLAN allocations)

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Sr. Infrastructure PM — GreenPeak Networks
lydia.park@greenpeak.com

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@greenpeak.com>
Cc: karty_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GreenPeak on-prem gateway: initial asks and diagram request

Thanks Lydia — this is the right level of detail. Short answers up front and then a proposed next step:

- Control-plane endpoints: api.cp.redwood.net (primary) and api-failover.cp.redwood.net (secondary). We can support either direct routable IPs or NAT behind your edge IPs; best practice is to present a routable NAT to avoid hairpinning for short-lived control connections.
- Telemetry: metrics.redwood.net:443 and logs.redwood.net:443 — allowlist by FQDN/IPs will be sufficient; we publish IP ranges 48 hours in advance.
- Certs/KMS: we support PKCS11-backed HSMs and AWS KMS. For on-prem we recommend bringing your PKI and issuing a client cert for the control-plane mutual TLS.
- BGP vs static: we strongly prefer BGP for data-plane failover and path-awareness; static is supported but requires manual failover scripts.

I'll attach our draft reference diagram (redwood-gateway-reference-2027-09-13.pdf) and an initial runway doc. Proposed next step: 30-min call Wed 9/15 10:00 PDT to walk diagrams and decide VLAN tags/ASN. If that works, we'll circulate an agenda.

Attaching: redwood-gateway-reference-2027-09-13.pdf

— Sergio Alvarez
Head of Field Engineering — Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Lydia / Sergio — adding operational detail and a proposed canary plan.

Quick summary of what we'll bring to the call:
- Reference diagrams: Gateway control/data demarc (attached gateway-runway-v1.pdf).
- Canary playbook: first 10 tenants, traffic shunt to internal staging, monitoring hooks (see canary-playbook.md).
- Observability: we will provide a temporary metrics endpoint and a tracing span that your NOC can validate in the first 30 minutes.
- Access model: we need a single classless prefix for control-plane NAT (minimum /28) and a pair of VLAN tags per colo for data-plane peering.

Action items before Wed call (owner):
1) GreenPeak: share VLAN tags + ASN for both colo sites (Lydia) — due EOD Tue.
2) Redwood: publish the control-plane FQDN cert thumbprints and pre-shared validation token (Marissa) — attached in runbook excerpt.
3) Karthik: confirm routing adjacency and BGP communities we suggest (Karthik) — will post a short note in the thread.

Attachments: gateway-runway-v1.pdf, canary-playbook.md

Thanks all — confirmed for Wed 9/15 10:00 PDT. Quick technical notes ahead of the call:

- BGP: we'll advertise only the tenant IP ranges to your routers. We recommend using AS prepends for staged failover and the following communities: 64512:10 (canary), 64512:20 (production).
- Control-plane NAT: a single public IP per colo with /28 is sufficient; we'll use TCP port 443, mTLS required.
- KV cache egress: short-lived signed tokens; please allow access to kvcache.redwood.net:443 from your edge.
- Observability: we'll produce a callout socket to your collector; exact IPs are in the drive link.

Next steps: run the 10-tenant canary on Thu 9/23 02:00 — 06:00 UTC (maintenance window proposed). Marissa will own the playbook execution; Sergio will own the rollback criteria.

See you on the call.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Network Engineer — Redwood Inference
